title: SAT Reading and Writing — Practice Mock 2

questions.question: Passage: Harlem Renaissance. The primary purpose of the passage is to
options: argue that jazz declined after the 1930s
describe the scope and legacy of the Harlem Renaissance
compare Hughes and Hurston's private lives
prove that white patrons controlled all Black art

questions.question: Hughes and Hurston treated Black experiences as
options: unworthy literary topics
worthy subjects for serious literature
topics only for European audiences
material that should avoid dialect

questions.question: The discussion of musicians mainly shows that artists
options: avoided commercial recording entirely
succeeded without facing structural barriers
shaped popular culture while confronting inequality
preferred segregated audiences

questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the scholars' debate?
options: Scholars disagree on details but agree on the movement's cultural impact.
The Renaissance failed to influence civil rights.
Militant essays were the only important texts of the era.
White publishers refused to print Black authors.

questions.question: The Great Depression is mentioned in order to
options: explain a factor that weakened institutional support
claim that Harlem's population disappeared
praise New Deal arts programs
argue that museums closed permanently

questions.question: As used in the passage, recover most nearly means
options: financially reimburse
restore to public attention
physically heal
copy without permission

questions.question: Which inference is best supported?
options: Harlem Renaissance artists agreed on every political strategy.
American modernism developed without Black creators.
Artistic innovation occurred alongside ongoing racial inequality.
Northern cities eliminated segregation by 1925.

questions.question: Which idea best supports lasting influence of the Renaissance?
options: Harlem became a center of artistic production in the 1920s.
The movement expanded audiences for Black art and trained creators who influenced later civil rights culture.
Musicians transformed popular entertainment.
The Great Depression reduced philanthropic support.
